paper_says.quote: Thirty-six percent of replications had statistically significant results
paper_says.where: Abstract of the paper. The authors' own script prints 35/97

spec.title: When psychology studies were repeated, how many held up? The Reproducibility Project said 36%
spec.statement: The Open Science Collaboration (Science, 2015) repeated 100 published psychology experiments. Of the 97 originals with significant results, 36% of the repeats were significant too. This recounts that share with our own small program on the project's public results table. It doesn't redo the experiments, and a mismatch ends as inconclusive.

source.license: Rebuild: MIT. Data: CC0, fetched from the project's OSF page, not redistributed.
source.authors: Open Science Collaboration; rebuild by the RERUN project

artifact.entrypoint: python reproducibility-project-2015/rebuild.py rpp_data.csv > rerun_output.txt && cat rerun_output.txt

metric.name: percent of repeated studies significant again

published_output_check: The authors' output file prints 35/97, which is 36.08%. The rebuild counts 35 of 97, 36.0825%.
